note: XXVII: the Count on the bridge — rising, struck, dust — silhouettes against the sun (Ian, 21 Nov)
style: An oil painting in colour of 1893 matching the first reference image: the same great ancient stone bridge with carved gargoyles over a deep snowy gorge, the same ruined castle on its crag, the same blood-red sunset sky with the sun low and large, in the manner of Thomas Cole. The figures are dark silhouettes against the setting sun, with detail only in the rim light. Strong value contrast, loose visible brushwork. No blood, no gore. No text, signature or border.

beats.text: Shot: wide, on the bridge deck. A long open rectangular wooden box lies overturned on the snowy paving, earth spilled out of it, and a tall gaunt figure in a long dark coat is rising from it onto his knees, one hand on the stones, a black silhouette against the huge setting sun. Around him on the bridge: men with levelled rifles, mounted gypsies in sheepskins reining back, a halted cart, all in silhouette with rim light, the carved balustrade and gargoyles catching the red light.

Shot: wide, on the bridge deck, silhouettes against the huge setting sun. Two men strike at the tall kneeling figure beside the overturned box: one sweeps a great curved blade in a flashing arc, the other drives a long knife downward; the kneeling figure arched back, all three black against the red disc of the sun, the other men and the gypsies frozen around them, the castle on its crag beyond.

Shot: wide, on the bridge deck at sunset. Where the tall figure knelt beside the overturned box there is only a drifting cloud of fine grey dust rising and dispersing into the red light of the setting sun, the two men standing back with their blades lowered, the others in silhouette around them, the castle beyond.
